courses.title: Modern Robotics: Mechanics, Planning, and Control
courses.zh: 机器人学基础：力学、规划与控制
courses.anchor: Lynch and Park; official book chapters 2–13

source_urls.title: Modern Robotics: official book, software and chapter outline

courses.scope: Core robot mechanics and motion methods, anchored to the actual book chapters. Modern Robotics does not comprehensively cover probabilistic estimation, advanced legged/robust/optimal control, modern reinforcement learning or robot-learning deployment engineering. Supplementary node links extend the foundations; they are not claims that every linked algorithm is taught in the book.

modules.title: Rigid-Body Motions

modules.title: Forward Kinematics

modules.title: Velocity Kinematics and Statics

modules.title: Inverse Kinematics

modules.title: Closed Chains

modules.title: Open-Chain Dynamics

modules.title: Trajectory Generation
modules.summary: Chapter 9: interpolation and time scaling.

modules.title: Motion Planning

modules.title: Robot Control
modules.summary: Chapter 11: motion, force and interaction control.
modules.learning_outcome: Choose feedback quantities and interpret tracking error dynamics.

modules.title: Grasping and Manipulation

modules.title: Wheeled Mobile Robots

nodes.title: 采样信号、混叠与滤波
nodes.summary: A sampled signal stores values at discrete times.
nodes.definition: A sampled signal stores values at discrete times. Sampling can make distinct continuous-time frequencies indistinguishable, which is aliasing. For an ideally band-limited signal, a sampling rate strictly above twice its highest frequency permits reconstruction under ideal assumptions. Physical sensor bandwidth, anti-aliasing filters, timestamp jitter and dropped samples complicate that result. A digital low-pass filter reduces selected frequency components but adds phase delay. Control and estimation must therefore account for both noise reduction and latency. Upsampling an already aliased recording cannot recover information that was lost during acquisition.
nodes.example: A 50 Hz stream cannot uniquely represent a 40 Hz sinusoid: it can appear as a 10 Hz component. Record sensor acquisition rate separately from policy update rate. Before downsampling IMU data, apply an appropriate anti-alias filter and quantify the resulting delay.
nodes.role_en: Sampling and filter delay connect sensor measurements, discretized feedback and trustworthy estimation.

notation.meaning: Sampling rate and highest retained frequency, hertz.
Smoothing coefficient between zero and one for this first-order filter.

nodes.title: 混杂动力学与接触模式
nodes.summary: A hybrid dynamical system combines continuous evolution with discrete changes of mode.
nodes.definition: A hybrid dynamical system combines continuous evolution with discrete changes of mode. In legged robotics, flight, left support, right support and double support can have different constraints. A guard condition specifies when a transition occurs, and a reset map describes an instantaneous state change such as impact velocity. Not every simulator explicitly exposes such modes: compliant contact models can instead resolve rapid transitions continuously. Identifying the intended formulation prevents confusing smooth control derivatives with derivatives across an impact. Mode timing and contact feasibility matter even when a trajectory looks kinematically smooth.
nodes.example: A foot approaches the ground during flight. At contact the normal gap reaches zero while the foot is approaching; an impact model can change velocity before stance dynamics begin. A reference motion with a stance foot sliding sideways violates its intended contact mode even when all joint angles are within limits.
nodes.role_en: Hybrid contact models connect constrained dynamics, gait phases, impact simulation and physically executable motion tracking.

nodes.en: Wrenches, Grasp Maps and Force Closure
nodes.title: 力旋量、抓取映射与力闭合
nodes.summary: A wrench combines a force and the moment it produces about a specified reference point.
nodes.definition: A wrench combines a force and the moment it produces about a specified reference point. A grasp map transforms individual contact forces into the net wrench on an object. Contact locations, contact types and friction restrict the set of achievable wrenches. Force closure means admissible contacts can counter arbitrary sufficiently small external wrenches in every direction; it is stronger than merely touching or holding an object against gravity in one pose. Frame conventions and units must be explicit because moment and force components have different dimensions. A geometrically feasible grasp can still violate actuator or friction limits.
nodes.example: Two opposed frictionless contacts on a flat-sided object may resist forces in one direction while failing to resist tangential slip or rotation. Add friction cones and actual contact locations before assessing wrench feasibility. A successful rendered grasp pose alone is not evidence of force closure.
nodes.role_en: Wrench feasibility extends friction and statics into grasp selection, manipulation and contact-force optimization.

notation.meaning: Wrench with moment first under the convention used here.
Admissible contact-force set, including friction constraints.

nodes.title: 轮式运动学与非完整约束
nodes.summary: A wheeled robot can have instantaneous velocity restrictions that do not remove the corresponding configuration coordinates.
nodes.definition: A wheeled robot can have instantaneous velocity restrictions that do not remove the corresponding configuration coordinates. An ideal differential-drive robot cannot translate sideways instantaneously, yet a sequence of forward motions and turns can reach a sideways-displaced pose. This is a nonholonomic constraint. Wheel radius, track width, frame orientation and sign conventions determine the mapping from wheel speeds to body motion. Odometry integrates that model and accumulates error when wheels slip or parameters are inaccurate. Kinematic reachability does not imply an arbitrary smooth pose trajectory can be tracked under wheel-speed and acceleration limits.
nodes.example: With equal wheel speeds a differential-drive robot moves straight; opposite wheel speeds rotate it. To reach a point directly to its left, it must turn and translate rather than command a lateral velocity that its rolling constraints forbid. Mecanum-wheel kinematics use a different model.
nodes.role_en: Nonholonomic models extend configuration-space planning, odometry and feedback to wheeled mobile robots.

notation.meaning: Wheel radius and wheel separation, metres.

nodes.title: 路径参数化与时间标定
nodes.summary: A geometric path specifies a sequence of configurations without stating when the robot reaches them.
nodes.definition: A geometric path specifies a sequence of configurations without stating when the robot reaches them. Time scaling supplies a monotonic path parameter as a function of time, producing velocity and acceleration. A collision-free path can violate joint-speed, acceleration or torque constraints when traversed too quickly. Smooth polynomial scaling can enforce endpoint velocity conditions, while time-optimal scaling seeks the shortest feasible duration under specified constraints. This problem differs from finding a new path or solving a general trajectory optimization problem, though the methods can be combined. Derivative continuity must match the controller and actuator requirements.
nodes.example: Move one joint along a fixed path from zero to one radian. A cubic timing law can start and finish at zero velocity, but its acceleration and torque still need checking. Doubling the duration reduces speed and acceleration while leaving the geometric path unchanged.
nodes.role_en: Time scaling connects motion planning to executable references for joint controllers and motion-tracking policies.

nodes.en: C++ Ownership, Compilation and Build Dependencies
nodes.title: C++ 所有权、编译与构建依赖
nodes.summary: Native robotics software often uses C++ for hardware interfaces, geometry and simulation.
nodes.definition: Native robotics software often uses C++ for hardware interfaces, geometry and simulation. The source code is compiled and linked against libraries before execution. Object lifetime and ownership determine whether referenced memory remains valid, and build configuration determines which headers, binaries and dependencies are used. A Python binding does not eliminate these native dependencies. Understanding compilation errors, linking errors and runtime library loading helps distinguish code problems from environment problems. Reproducibility requires recording compiler and dependency versions along with the build options. A fast executable still needs correct synchronization, tested interfaces and measured timing.
nodes.example: A Python process importing a simulator can fail because its native shared library was built against an incompatible dependency. Another error arises when a C++ callback retains a reference after the original object has been destroyed. These require different diagnoses from a Python syntax error.
nodes.role_en: Native ownership and build knowledge support ROS 2 packages, simulator extensions and reliable high-rate control integrations.

notation.meaning: Resolve compiled symbols and library dependencies.

nodes.en: Version Control, Regression Tests and CI
nodes.title: 版本控制、回归测试与持续集成
nodes.summary: Version control records source changes and allows a tested implementation to be identified precisely.
nodes.definition: Version control records source changes and allows a tested implementation to be identified precisely. Automated tests check specified behavior at different scopes: a unit test can verify one transform, while an integration test checks a sensor-to-controller interface. A regression test preserves a previously corrected behavior. Continuous integration runs selected checks on new changes in a controlled environment. Passing tests supports only the cases and assumptions they exercise; it does not prove physical safety or research generalization. Test data, tolerances and dependencies must be recorded alongside the source revision to make failures interpretable.
nodes.example: A frame-conversion test verifies that a known camera point transforms correctly into the robot frame. An integration replay then checks timestamp handling with delayed messages. Neither test establishes ball-contact success on hardware, which requires a separate experiment and measured outcomes.
nodes.role_en: Versioned tests connect software changes, reproducible training configurations and evidence for deployable robot behavior.

notation.meaning: The scope actually supported by executed checks.

nodes.en: Robot Data Recording, Replay and Provenance
nodes.title: 机器人数据记录、回放与来源
nodes.summary: A robot recording should preserve observations, commands, timestamps, coordinate frames and the configuration required to interpret them.
nodes.definition: A robot recording should preserve observations, commands, timestamps, coordinate frames and the configuration required to interpret them. Replay feeds recorded data into software to reproduce an input sequence. It helps isolate perception or interface regressions, but replay does not recreate closed-loop physical interaction unless the environment response is modeled. A changed controller would have produced different future observations on the real robot. Record acquisition time separately from arrival time, and identify missing messages or clock discontinuities. Dataset provenance also includes sensor calibration, robot variant, policy version and any filtering or resampling.
nodes.example: Replay a recorded camera and IMU stream through two estimators using the same calibration and timestamps. Compare pose residuals and latency. This supports an estimator comparison on that recorded sequence; it does not demonstrate how a changed policy would steer the robot through a new physical encounter.
nodes.role_en: Recording and replay connect ROS 2 timing, datasets, debugging and repeatable perception evaluation.

notation.meaning: Configuration and provenance needed to interpret the sample.

nodes.en: Runtime Fault Detection and Controller Lifecycle
nodes.title: 运行故障检测与控制器生命周期
nodes.summary: A runtime controller needs defined behavior when observations become stale, an update misses its deadline, a command is invalid or hardware reports an error.
nodes.definition: A runtime controller needs defined behavior when observations become stale, an update misses its deadline, a command is invalid or hardware reports an error. Lifecycle states make activation, operation, fallback and shutdown explicit. A watchdog monitors whether required updates arrive on time; it does not determine that every received command is correct. Fallback behavior must be appropriate to the robot state and tested through the actual interface. A generic zero command can have different meanings for torque, velocity and position control. Logging the triggering condition and state transition makes a fault response auditable.
nodes.example: If the policy stops producing actions, detect the elapsed command age and switch through a documented controller transition. For a humanoid, abruptly disabling torque and commanding a held pose are physically different responses. Evaluate the intended fallback first with injected software faults in simulation and controlled integration tests.
nodes.role_en: Fault semantics connect control deadlines, command units, hardware interfaces and observable deployment behavior.

nodes.en: Actuator Dynamics, Torque–Speed and Thermal Limits
nodes.title: 执行器动力学、转矩速度与热限制
nodes.summary: A commanded joint torque is realized through a motor, transmission, drive electronics and control loop.
nodes.definition: A commanded joint torque is realized through a motor, transmission, drive electronics and control loop. An ideal motor approximation relates torque to current, but available voltage, speed, current limits, friction and heating restrict actual output. Continuous torque can be lower than a short peak rating, and a fixed URDF effort limit cannot represent every torque-speed or thermal dependency. Actuator delay and bandwidth also change tracking and stability. Identify the command interface, gear convention and measurement frame before fitting or learning a dynamics model. Simulated actuator parameters should be validated against the intended hardware operating conditions.
nodes.example: A controller can request an allowed peak torque at high joint speed while the motor cannot supply it because of voltage limits. Repeatedly holding that torque can also exceed thermal limits. Domain randomization of mass alone does not account for these actuator differences.
nodes.role_en: Actuator dynamics connect motor hardware, system identification, simulator action models and sim-to-real control.
